title: Eden, read on 2026-10-07: two brands under one name, and why nothing was written
keys: Each product is keyed as it stood at the end of the second walk. Stage c8 changed no product.
decidedBy: The owner, 2026-10-07: Eden is two brands with the same name. The session of stage c8 then found that the registry cannot hold that, and stopped.
why: brands.key is unique (index uq_brands_key) and the key is brandKey(label), so a second brand whose label is "Eden" answers 409. A homonym (plan 0178) is a pointer from the printed key "eden" to a second brand that has ANOTHER label and key, as "Poseidon Food" is beside "Poseidon". A product takes its brand from the text that is written on it, by key, so the 16 products can only move to a brand whose label is not "Eden". The label is shown to shoppers and the owner did not choose one, so nothing was written.
whatItTakes: The owner names the second brand (a label whose key is not "eden", for example the legal or range name of the shoe care business).
POST /v1/admin/catalog/brands { "label": "<that label>" } creates it. linkedItems must be 0.
POST /v1/admin/catalog/brands/<new id>/homonyms { "printedKey": "eden" } makes a queue row that prints EDEN answer both brands in brandMatches, the bathroom brand first.
PATCH /v1/admin/catalog/items/batch (or the single item route) with brand = "<that label>" on the 16 ids below. The WC product is not sent.
Or: a change of the model so that two registry rows can hold one label. That is a migration, and it moves the restore manifest.
